title: The Consonants and Their Clusters
subtitle: C and G (hard/soft), H (silent), SC, GL, GN, and the affricates.
objectives: Pronounce c and g hard before a, o, u; soft before e, i.
Understand that h is silent but ch and gh restore the hard sound.
Master sc before e, i (like English sh in shoe).
Pronounce gli (like the lli in million) and gn (like the ny in canyon).

sections.heading: C and G: hard and soft
sections.body: In Italian, c before a, o, u is hard: casa, cosa, cura. Before e, i it softens to ch as in church: cento, cinema. Same rule for g: hard before a, o, u (gatto, gola, gusto); soft before e, i (gente, giro). The letter h is silent in Italian. But when placed after c or g, it forces the hard sound before e or i: che (not che but ke), chi; ghe, ghi. Examples: perché (why), laghi (lakes).

letters.note: Palatalized double l, like the lli in million. figlio, gli.
Palatalized n, like the ny in canyon. ogni, sogno.

sections.heading: Examples from Dante
sections.body: Dante Alighieri, Inferno I.1: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita. Read it aloud. cammin: double m, hard c. nostra: hard c implied in the cluster str. vita: single consonants, open i. Petrarch, Canzoniere 1: Voi ch'ascoltate in rime sparse il suono. ch' equals che (hard k sound). ascoltate: sc before o is hard. sparse: no cluster, but note the open a.

sections.heading: Listening drill
sections.instructions: Minimal pairs and clusters. Repeat each one after the recording.

items.prompt: What sound does sc make before e or i?

items.answer: palatalized ll, like the lli in million.
palatalized n, like the ny in canyon.

items.prompt: Why is h used in chi and che?
items.answer: To force the hard k sound before e and i, where c would otherwise soften to ch.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark complete when you can read any Italian word aloud with correct c/g hard/soft and palatals.
